content:
Very fun, very short, and very simple. I think this a great idea, and would work really well.

However, I think you should correct the grammar in the statement though. Maybe reword it to something like, "You need to analyze <<the quality of>> [[n]] <<metals>>, where [[t]] is the minimum purity, [[p]], required to <<pass the quality test>>. Output {{keep}} if the metal passes the test, or {{discard}} if it doesn't. At the end, output the indexes of the selected metals, all separated by a space, ranging from 0 to [[n]] - 1.

In the "Next n lines" part of the input, you should add [[p]] right after purity.

In the output, keep and discard should probably be formatted as {{keep}} and {{discard}}.

Also, in the constraints, you should add a constraint on the variable n.

Lastly, I don't know if this is great for reverse mode just because of the last part of the question. I don't know how easy this is to figure out within 5-10 minutes, but I'll leave this up to you.

In addition to what @Compootah wrote:

Input
* Next n lines: Please change "The" to "An integer [[p]], representing the".

Output
* Please remove the quotation marks after formatting "keep" and "discard".

* Please change "Line n + 1" to "Next line".

Thanks.
Thanks, I put the changes in. If there's anything else let me know
